title: Croatia denied visas to nine Russian gymnasts, then admitted four. One of them, Angelina Melnikova, later won gold.
text: Croatia denied visas to nine Russian gymnasts, then admitted four. One of them, Angelina Melnikova, later won gold. August 14, 2026, 12:06 am Source: Meduza Russian gymnast Angelina Melnikova won the individual all-around title at the 2026 European Championships in artistic gymnastics, held in Croatia, scoring 55.932 points. Russian gymnast Anna Kalmykova took second place with 54.632 points, and French gymnast Elena Colas placed third with 53.966 points. The competitors performed on the uneven bars, balance beam, vault, and floor exercise. The win made Melnikova a five-time European champion in artistic gymnastics and gave her the first individual all-around title of her career. She had previously won gold in the team event in 2016 and 2018, on the floor exercise in 2017, and on the uneven bars in 2021. Melnikova is also an Olympic champion — she won gold in the team event in 2020 — and a three-time world champion. This is the first time in five years that Russian gymnasts are competing at the European Championships, doing so under neutral status. text: Russian strikes kill one, injure 15 in Ukraine’s Kramatorsk area August 14, 2026, 12:01 am Source: Vadym Filashkin On the evening of August 13, Russian forces launched several aerial bomb strikes on the city of Kramatorsk and the village of Bilenke in the Donetsk region, Governor Vadym Filashkin said. The strikes damaged a multistory apartment building in Kramatorsk. Photos and video of the aftermath show that part of the building collapsed and a fire broke out. Filashkin said the strikes killed one person and injured 15 others in the Kramatorsk community. It was not clear from his statement whether the casualties were connected to the partially destroyed building in Kramatorsk. title: Australia news live: Jacinta Allan to quit politics; Sydney airport near-miss distance was ‘substantial’ 1.3km, Airservices says
text: 21.40 EDT Jacinta Allan to quit politics Victoria’s recently deposed Labor premier, Jacinta Allan, has announced she will leave politics at the next election. In a statement today – posted to her social media pages along with a picture of her at 25 years old – Allan announced she would not recontest the seat of Bendigo in November. Allan said: In my first speech to Parliament, I said I wanted to be a representative who cared about people and listened to them … I finished that speech with a promise: ‘I intend to make a difference.’ Today, almost 27 years later, I have announced that I will not recontest the seat of Bendigo East at November’s election. But I look around the place I have called home my entire life and know that, together, we did make a difference. Allan listed what she saw as her achievements during her time in politics, and said: Politics has changed a lot since this photo was taken. So have I … And when I leave Parliament, I’ll leave the same way I arrived. A daughter of Bendigo. A daughter of workers. A proud Labor woman. Still believing in equality. title: Trump orders Pentagon to scrap modern jet launching tech on new US aircraft carrier and revert to steam catapults – as it happened
text: 20.06 EDT White House releases Trump's order to install steam catapults on new US aircraft carrier The White House has released the full text of a memorandum from Donald Trump to Pete Hegseth , the defense secretary, ordering a change in the construction of a new US Navy aircraft carrier, to replace the electromagnetic aircraft launch system with steam catapults. The supposed superiority of steam catapults for launching fighter jets has been an obsession of the president’s since 2017 when, he says, he was convinced by a single conversation with a Navy officer that the electromagnetic system installed in modern aircraft carriers was too complex. The presidential memorandum, titled, “Rebuilding the United States Navy and America’s Shipbuilding Industrial Base”, claims to address “a series of shipbuilding setbacks stemming from overly complex designs” for US Navy ships. Section 2 of the memo includes the order to change the construction of the USS Doris Miller, a Ford-class aircraft carrier known as CVN-81, which is already two years behind schedule : Sec. 2.
